records.name: Dolce Suono Ensemble
records.summary: A chamber music group that puts on concerts in Philadelphia, tours, and commissions new pieces. Audiences come to the concert series, and the group also runs community partnerships.
records.what_you_do: Buy a ticket to a concert on the home series, or come to one of the composer and young artist events.

schedule.text: Home concert series in Philadelphia. The site lists a June 14, 2026 concert and announces a 2026 to 2027 season, with dates not shown on the page.

cost.text: Ticket prices not listed on the page

first_step.how: Buy a ticket to the next home concert listed on the Concerts and Tickets page at dolcesuono.com
first_step.basis: Concerts are public and ticketed, so anyone can attend

records.notes: No tag fits chamber music exactly, so community_band is the closest choice. The site shows no street address; the batch address (135 N 22nd St) is unconfirmed. Email on the contact page is obscured, so it is not recorded. The June 14, 2026 item is a concert date; the post date is not shown.

records.name: Orchestra 2001, Inc.
records.summary: A Philadelphia ensemble that plays new and 20th and 21st century classical music and jazz. Its Playing the Markets pop-ups bring small groups into shops, markets and workplaces, and its concerts are open to the public.
records.what_you_do: Catch a free or low cost pop-up performance, buy a concert ticket, or ask about volunteering through the group's website.

schedule.text: Playing the Markets pop-ups and concert series throughout the year. Recent listed dates: Sept 24, 2026 (Fairmount Farmers Market) and Oct 3, 2026 (Firstival at Eastern State Penitentiary).

cost.text: Varies: some events are free or pay what you wish, others are $10 to $25

first_step.how: Watch orchestra2001.org for the next Playing the Markets pop-up near you, or email info@orchestra2001.org to ask about volunteering
first_step.basis: Pop-ups are public and free or low cost; the site lists a volunteer role

records.notes: The site lists a volunteer role but describes no volunteer schedule. No tag fits exactly, so community_band is used as closest. Mailing address (P.O. Box 7211) not recorded; the Cherry Street Pier address is the public physical address. Musicians' login pages were not used.

records.name: Philadelphia Sculptors
records.summary: A group of sculptors that runs exhibitions, public forums and a members gallery to make sculpture more visible in the city. Visitors see the shows, and members show their work online and in exhibitions.
records.what_you_do: Visit the current exhibition or studio tour, and join as a member to show your own sculpture in the online gallery.

schedule.text: Exhibitions run in blocks. Re:Form runs Oct 2 to 30, 2026 at Art on the Ave, with the Philadelphia Open Studio Tour on Oct 10 and 11 from noon to 6 pm.

cost.text: Exhibition admission not stated. Tax-deductible donations are accepted.

first_step.how: Go to Re:Form at Art on the Ave, 3808 Lancaster Ave, before it closes Oct 30, or to the Open Studio Tour on Oct 10 or 11
first_step.basis: Exhibitions and the studio tour are public; membership is the route to showing work

records.notes: Batch address said Suite 300; the site says Suite 320, so the site is used. No classes or volunteer roles are listed. Membership cost is not published. Facebook page exists but its URL is not given on the site, so it is not recorded. The opening reception (Oct 2) has already passed.

records.name: Shakespeare in Clark Park
records.summary: A theater company that puts on Shakespeare plays outdoors in Clark Park each summer. Audiences come to the shows, and the company posts job openings for artists on its site.
records.what_you_do: Come to a summer show in Clark Park. The company lists paid job openings under Work with Us; it does not describe volunteer roles.

schedule.text: Outdoor summer productions in Clark Park. Hamlet is listed for summer 2026; the page gives no dates.

cost.text: Ticket prices are not published on the site

first_step.how: Check shakespeareinclarkpark.org for the next season's dates, then go to a show in Clark Park
first_step.basis: Shows are public outdoor performances; ticket rules are not confirmed

records.notes: Batch address (627 N 18th St Apt 302) looks like a private apartment, so it is not published; the venue is Clark Park. The 2025 Barrymore Award and summer 2026 Hamlet are dated only by year. The site's newsletter sign-up shows a placeholder error, so it may not work.

records.name: Tempesta di Mare, Inc.
records.summary: A Philadelphia baroque orchestra that plays music from about 300 years ago and digs up works that were forgotten. Audiences attend a season of recitals and orchestra concerts, and the group lists a Young Friends program and a Baroque Music 101 program.
records.what_you_do: Attend a recital or orchestra concert. The group also lists a Young Friends program and a Baroque Music 101 program; details are not on the page.

schedule.text: 2026 to 2027 season of recital and orchestra concerts. Listed dates: Adam Pearl harpsichord Oct 30 to Nov 1, Karen Dekker violin Nov 12 to 15, A German Advent Dec 18 to 20.

cost.text: Ticket prices are not listed; single tickets and season tickets are offered

first_step.how: Buy a single ticket for the Adam Pearl harpsichord recital (Oct 30 to Nov 1) or the Karen Dekker violin recital (Nov 12 to 15) at tempestadimare.org
first_step.basis: Ticketed public concerts; anyone can buy a single ticket

records.notes: No tag fits baroque orchestra exactly, so community_band is used as closest. Venues are on a Venues and Logistics page that was not read, so no address is recorded. The Sept 24, 2026 blog post is the newest dated item. The Oct 30 to Nov 1 year is not printed on each date; it falls in the 2026 to 2027 season.

records.name: East Falls Forward (The Fallser Club)
records.notes: This is a music venue and event space that does business as The Fallser Club. Its public way in is buying tickets to shows. The site lists no classes, volunteer roles, membership or dated events, and it has no phone or email on the page. Verdict not_a_group because it is a venue. Revisit if the event calendar or a community program is published with dates.

records.name: Jazz Bridge Project
records.summary: Helps Jazz and Blues musicians in the Philadelphia area who are in money, health or housing trouble, with a social worker and emergency grants. It also hosts free neighborhood concerts played by local jazz musicians.
records.what_you_do: Musicians in crisis can ask for help through the group. Anyone can attend the free neighborhood concerts or give a donation.

schedule.text: Free neighborhood concerts: Nov 19, 2026 in Collingswood, Dec 2, 2026 in Cheltenham, Mar 4, 2027 in Collingswood, May 5, 2027 in Cheltenham, and May 6, 2027 in Collingswood.

cost.text: Concerts are free to attend. Donations are accepted.

first_step.how: Come to a free concert, such as the Dec 2, 2026 show in Cheltenham, or email info@jazzbridge.org if you are a musician who needs help
first_step.basis: Concerts are free and public; musician help is requested by contacting the group

records.notes: Site address (6703 Germantown Ave, Suite 200) differs from the city list (4323 Main St); the site address is used. Concerts are held in Cheltenham and Collingswood, NJ, which are outside Philadelphia. The last sign of life is the published concert schedule, which shows no publish date. No tag fits exactly for concerts, so jam_sessions is used.
